title: What is known about 1RB1RA_1RC1LB, and what is open
description: Proof status of the six-state machine 1RB1RA_1RC1LB_1LD0RA_---0LE_1LC0LF_1RE0LB: what is proved in Lean, what is computed, what is only observed.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape. This page tracks what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
The work has just started: the shared tools are in place and the run has been looked at. Nearly everything about its structure is still observation.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves that the machine does not halt in its first 10,000,000 steps (the first 20,000 checked by Lean's kernel alone), and two shift rules that hold for every block length. A direct simulation finds no halt in the first 1010 steps.

The only halting transition is D reading 0, and D is entered only from C reading 0, so a halt needs C to meet two 0s in a row. The run keeps its tape as blocks of ones separated by single 0s during its rightward sweeps (and by 00 when the head is back at the left end): finding the rules that act on these blocks is the next step.

claims.title: No halt in 20,000 steps
claims.text: From blank tape the machine makes 20,000 steps without halting. Evaluated by Lean's kernel on a list simulator proved to agree with the machine's semantics.

claims.title: Two shift rules
claims.text: State A runs right over a block of n ones in n steps; state B runs left over a block of n ones to the 0 before it in n + 1 steps; for every n and any surrounding tape.

claims.title: No halt in 10 million steps
claims.text: The same statement for 10,000,000 steps, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: A direct simulation in C runs 10<sup>10</sup> steps without a halt (137,072 ones on the tape then). The simulator is tested against the Python reference simulator and on machines with known step counts.

claims.title: No simple conserved quantity
claims.text: No quantity a·(number of 1s) + b·(head position) + W[state] is conserved modulo any m from 2 to 12. (The other machine has one modulo 3, which the same search finds.)

claims.title: The tape is a list of blocks
claims.text: Seen in the run: blocks of ones separated by single 0s during rightward sweeps, by 00 (a 000 after the first block) when the head is back at the left end.

claims.title: Returns to the left end
claims.text: The left end of the visited tape moves out 15 times, the last at step 2,047,931, and then not again up to 10<sup>10</sup> steps. Between returns the first block roughly halves.

claims.title: The block rules
claims.text: What one sweep does to the list of block lengths, as rules proved for every length.

claims.title: Whether it halts
claims.text: Whether the run from blank tape ever brings C onto two 0s in a row.
